w:r.w:t: Test Specification - 01: General Modules (Web and Mobile)
Shared Authentication, Accounts, Content, Progress, Security, and Support
Verify workflows and authoritative data shared by the ARTICTON web and mobile systems.
Google Chrome / Microsoft Edge and Android / iOS devices or emulators
1. Attempt login on web and mobile using the same valid account.
2. Repeat with an incorrect password and an unknown account.
Both clients accept the valid credentials and reject invalid credentials without creating a session. Error messages remain clear and consistent.
Apply role-based access across both clients
1. Sign in as student, faculty/staff, and administrator on each supported client.
2. Review the landing view and available actions.
Each role reaches only its authorized dashboard and tools. Restricted actions are hidden or denied on both platforms.
2. Restart/refresh the client and verify session restoration.
3. Sign out and attempt to reopen a protected view.
An active valid session is restored. Signing out clears access, returns to authentication, and prevents protected data from reopening.
3. Open the same account on the other client.
Valid first name, last name, and supported profile values
The saved profile belongs only to the current user and the same authoritative value appears on web and mobile.
1. Complete a supported assessment on one client.
2. Open the progress/dashboard view on the other client.
The server stores one authoritative result and both clients show matching score, pass/fail state, and progress without duplicate credit.
Publish approved learning content to both clients
1. Submit a module or question change as faculty.
3. Open the affected content on web and mobile.
Valid change request and administrator approval
Only approved content is published, and both clients load the same current revision while rejected/stale requests do not publish.
1. Attempt to read or modify another user's private data as a student.
3. Repeat the intended operation with an authorized role.
Unauthorized reads/writes are denied on both platforms; authorized operations succeed and expose only the fields required for the workflow.
Submit and manage shared support requests
1. Submit a valid support request from an available student client.
2. Open the admin support queue on web.
Name, email, subject, message, optional screenshot
One ticket is created through the approved workflow, appears in the admin queue, and moves from Open to In progress to Resolved.

Test Specification - 03: Mobile Application Test Cases
ARTICTON Flutter Mobile Learning and Assessment Application
Verify mobile navigation, four learning modules, server-backed assessments, progress, practice exams, and role tools.
Android and iOS phone/tablet devices or emulators
Restore a mobile session from the splash screen
1. Sign in and close the application.
2. Reopen the application with the account still authenticated.
The splash screen restores a valid server-backed profile and opens the correct account scope. After sign-out, it opens the login flow.
1. Open the student dashboard in portrait.
2. Navigate through Dashboard, Modules, Exams, and Profile.
3. Rotate to landscape or use a wide device.
Portrait uses the bottom navigation bar; wide/landscape uses the navigation rail. The selected page and readable layout remain stable.
2. Visit Module 1: PC Parts, Module 2: Disassembly, Module 3: Assembly, and Module 4: Software & Networking.
Each module displays its correct title and content. Approved content is preferred, and the app remains usable when starter content is used.
Start a supported pre-test or post-test
1. Open a module pre-test or post-test.
3. Verify question text and two to four options.
One of the eight module assessment IDs
Supported assessments create a server attempt with valid questions. Unsupported IDs are rejected before a callable request is made.
Submit assessment answers and calculate results
3. Compare correct count, total, percentage, and pass state.
The server result is shown and clamped to 0-100. Invalid answer indexes are rejected. A module post-test reaches Passed at 70% or higher.
1. Finish the guided content for a module.
3. Return to the dashboard and reopen progress.
Completion is sent through the protected completeGuidedModule callable and the dashboard reflects the saved content component for that user.
1. Complete a pre-test, module content, and post-test.
3. Compare displayed module and overall percentages.
Progress uses 20% pre-test, 50% content completion, and 30% post-test percentage. The overall value is the rounded average of four modules.
Open mobile practice exams under the configured gate
1. Open Exams below and above 70% overall progress.
2. Test Practice Exam 1 and Practice Exam 2.
3. Repeat with the development bypass setting noted.
Production configuration locks exams below 70% and unlocks them at 70%. The current development bypass permits testing and is clearly treated as non-production behavior.
Edit profile, submit support, and sign out
Profile changes save for the current account, the support request is accepted, and sign-out clears navigation history and returns to login.
Switch theme and preserve readable UI
1. Switch between light and dark modes.
2. Navigate across Dashboard, Modules, Exams, and Profile.
Theme selection applies consistently, text and controls remain readable, and the selected mode persists according to the theme controller.
Use faculty mobile content and question editors
Valid cards, summary, questions, options, answers, and explanations
Valid requests are saved for admin review; incomplete or invalid assessment data is rejected and does not publish directly.
Review mobile approval queues as administrator
3. Approve one current request and reject another.
Approved content becomes the published revision, rejected content remains unpublished, and stale/already-reviewed requests cannot overwrite newer data.
